limitations: Trained and evaluated on PPG-DaLiA (terrestrial, free-living daily activities), not astronaut or spaceflight data - no microgravity validation.

Held-out test set is 3 subjects (out of 15 total) in this specific seeded split - a different split could shift exact numbers, though the direction of the effect (IMU helps) was consistent across all 3 test subjects individually.

IMU benefit did NOT monotonically increase with motion-quartile severity in this run (largest absolute gain was in the lowest-motion quartile) - reported as observed, not smoothed into a monotonic story.
Per-activity breakdown shows one activity (table_soccer) where Model B performed WORSE than Model A - a real negative result within an overall-positive experiment.
CURRENT MODEL DOES NOT PROVIDE VALIDATED PREDICTIVE UNCERTAINTY. Model output is a single point estimate; no variance/confidence head exists or has been calibrated.
This experiment establishes heart-rate estimation performance only - it does not establish anything about stress, fatigue, cognitive load, or other targets.

ModalityFusionTransformer was generalized during this experiment to accept an explicit n_modalities parameter (previously hard-coupled to the dashboard's global 4-modality tuple) - default behavior for existing dashboard callers is unchanged and covered by backend/tests/test_models.py.

robustness_evidence.imu_calibration_caveat: IMU noise and saturation scales came from the first affected S14 batch, whose motion variance was much lower than typical later windows; the tested grid is not proof of robustness to severe corruption.
robustness_evidence.packet_loss_interpretation: Independent loss of a required native-rate sample primarily triggered fail-closed input rejection, so packet-loss results characterize prediction availability rather than continuous error degradation.
robustness_evidence.supported_claim: Observed behavior of the frozen canonical pipeline under controlled corruption of official held-out S14 replay data.

limitations: Held-out subject s2 has a real HR distribution far outside the training population's range (verified from raw R-peak data: sit ~121bpm, run ~140bpm mean, vs. a train-set mean of ~85bpm) - a genuine out-of-distribution subject that dominates the small (N=4) held-out aggregate for both models. Not excluded from the frozen result per pre-registered protocol; disclosed here as context, not as grounds to recompute the headline metric.
Candidate configuration has strictly more input channels (6 vs 3) than baseline by construction - channel-count and site-value effects are not perfectly separable.
